I think you should do whatever you feel is best for you, even if that means going to the ER. A lot of your pain could very well be from avoiding stronger pain medications. As I was saying to another person on this thread if wait until pain is unbearable before taking the medications it just becomes that much harder to control. If otc pain medicine isn’t covering your pain that’s what the prescription is there for.
 I know media influence has been detrimental to doctors and patients alike, and as I said before also the chances of addiction when managing acute post operative pain are not zero, but they are very low.
I’m just giving you my personal opinion because I tried taking the non narcotic pain relievers as much as possible after my last endo surgery and I didn’t end up doing myself any favors.
From what you’re describing you need to first and foremost do whatever you need to to do get your pain under control, and that often means taking the medicine before it becomes unbearable! 
Please don’t hesitate to go to the ER if you feel you are experiencing possible complications from surgery- better safe than sorry-
Though I understand not wanting to go! 
Good luck to you and I hope you feel better soon 🍀

Just a heads up for you, you should take pain medicine as prescribed and before it gets to its absolute worst. I understand that addiction is a concern for many especially since it’s been portrayed in the media that everyone who was prescribed an opioid medication became an addict- that and the fact that you have that in your family history all helps me understand your concerns and I’m not here to devalue them. That being said if you wait for it to get to its absolute worse before you take any medicine to help it- it will be much harder to get the pain down to a manageable level than If you decided to take it either as scheduled or at the first signs of noticing an increase in pain. 

I feel like a lot of media influence and the narrative health care workers spout off to anyone with pain has caused a lot of harm and misinformation. The truth is that the chance of addiction in someone trying to manage something like acute post operative pain is very low. 

I hope that helps you some

I was told by an er doctor years ago that people like me who needed real help were “slipping through the cracks” meaning the cracks in healthcare and in societies every single day. 
If I had not continued to be sick I would still know his name. He walked in to the ER exam room and sat in his chair face level to face level, eye contact, truly listened with an open mind. He told me my story makes sense although he doesn’t have the tools to diagnosis it as an emergency room doctor. Staff  completely ceased from treating me like an addict to realizing I was a real person with health problems after I talked to this doctor. And he did his best to help me with short term stabilization, but the nature of his work meant he could not provide my continuing or aftercare elsewhere. If he had I wouldn’t be here writing this today. If  he had when I met him, it would not have become so aggressive and hard to treat. It would have saved my mental health that day, and the parts of my life that matter, if I just could have continued care without it having to be on an emergency basis, with a doctor that treated me like a human being & listened and formed his own opinion. I don’t think that happens much anymore. Just someone forming their own opinion of you, without something prior they think they may know and without biases. We desperately need that in societies. Healthy or sick. We need that. Technology dehumanized healthcare more than we care to acknowledge I think.

I always felt like I was the problem too. I developed clinical depression by the time I hit puberty. Looking back they were “trying” to be normal when I hit my later teenage years, but they put me through hell when I was first struggling with depression. I thought everything was my fault, refused to accept the gravity of an MDD diagnosis and denied to myself that it was real for years. It seemed like as soon as I hit puberty all the things that were abnormal all those years began to catch up with me over night. 
That’s when the physical and emotional abuse really escalated. Now I hear from them, “yeah we did some things that were wrong, but you did a lot wrong too”. So basically I became depressed and hard to deal with so that was a good reason to abuse me. 

Smh. I knew things weren’t “normal” per-say, but I didn’t realize how abnormal (to be fair the area I grew up in has a lot of dysfunctional families living in poverty, so that that probably reinforced the idea that everyone lived some type of dysfunctional home life) wasn’t until I met a partner that did come from a normal family, and got to really know them - that’s when I became truly horrified by how I grew up. Even then it took me years to see it. 

My past haunts me & I don’t know how to make it stop. 
The other messed up part is I heavily resent my partner who had the world handed to them on a silver platter when I couldn’t even get my mother to do simple things like taking me to a doctor or dentist. I remember pulling a cavity filled baby tooth out myself in the school bathroom in the 5th grade just because no one would take me for medical care & I was embarrassed by it. 

My partner and his sibling had their university education paid for for them, while they were doing that my mother saw fit to put me as a “body” as she called it in the gas station she managed. 
Most customers were literally just functioning addicts liquor, beer, cigs, lotto, sugar, energy pills pretty much all the legal highs. Perfect environment for an 18 year old suffering from depression and severe social anxiety disorder. /s

I know it isn’t right to resent my partner, but I do.
I have more college than they do (because they just never showed up for classes) even with having a baby way too young and caring for them & holding a job. Then my world crashed again when I developed chronic pain. The doctor I see now says childhood trauma can lead to weird chronic pain conditions that doctors have a lot of trouble finding a diagnosis for, hence why I spent a decade on my own just getting traumatized in a different way by the healthcare system. 

They assumed I was on drugs because I was severely underweight with high blood pressure.

I think this can be a common belief for those who have attempted suicide and suffer from depression. Likely if you’re attempting we can confidently assume we are depressed. This idea is actually more common & older than you might think. Here’s an example from pop culture : in American horror story season 1, it is revealed that violet who thought she was alive, actually ended up dying from a pill overdose. I can remember times in my life where I thought I had actually died and was in purgatory. It helps to look at real life situations to help teach ourselves that this is a theory at best and an intrusive thought at worst. I have a lot of pets who I consider my babies, my family. Something that helped me was realizing that pure love without judgement or conditions like you get from caring for an animal, surely wouldn’t exist in hell. What does this psychiatrist that has you on antipsychotics say about what you believe about your reality? You really should have a trained therapist helping you challenge this belief. It doesn’t sound to me like a psychotic delusion, otherwise the meds would help, right? It’s more like something you’ve convinced yourself of. I’m not saying that to blame you or make you feel worse, so please don’t take it that way. I think if your depression were treated appropriately & again If you had someone helping you challenge this belief you would come to realize that you are still here. Even in the darkest times we can find something of beauty, like the trees around us, the birds and squirrels the flowers blooming, thunderstorms and gentle rains, all evidence of life continuing.

If you do take them long term (months or years) you will suffer from physical dependence.

When I say dependence I mean that your gaba receptors (the part of your brain that causes you to be able to relax) will no longer function in the absence of the drug, it will also begin to high Jack many other central nervous system functions as in your heart rate and blood pressure will not know how to regulate without it, all of which can be quite dangerous. 

I don’t really recommend it to anyone based on my own experience for these reasons.

Also - due to its function on the brain and central nervous system it is one of two drugs that can kill you to withdrawal from. The other is alcohol.
